The root cause of the issue is in the `get_module_members` method of the `ModuleDocumenter` class. This method does not handle an empty `__all__` attribute correctly. Specifically, it does not check if `__all__` is defined and is not empty before adding members to the `members` dictionary.

Currently, the `get_module_members` method iterates over all attributes in the module using `dir(self.object)` and adds them to the `members` dictionary without checking if `__all__` is defined or if it is an empty list. As a result, all members are included in the documentation, even when `__all__` is explicitly set to an empty list.

#### Expected Behavior
When `__all__` is defined and is an empty list, no members should be included in the documentation. The `get_module_members` method should check if `__all__` is defined and is not empty before adding members to the `members` dictionary.

The problematic code is located in the `get_module_members` method of the `ModuleDocumenter` class in the file `sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py`.

#### Suggested Fix
A suggested fix is to add a check for an empty `__all__` and return an empty dictionary if it is defined and is an empty list. Here is the proposed change:
